channel.title: WireMinute | Breaking News & Live World Updates
channel.description: Breaking news and live world updates from WireMinute: world, politics, business, technology, sports and health, reported in our own words and updated every minute.

item.title: Zelenskyy Says Calling Putin a Friend Is Like Calling Hitler a Friend
item.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said it is strange for Donald Trump to call Vladimir Putin his friend, likening it to calling Adolf Hitler a friend during the Second World War.

item.title: Goyal Says India-US Trade Deal Is Nearly Done as Tariff Threat Hangs Over Talks
item.description: India's commerce minister says a long-delayed trade agreement with Washington is close to being finished, days after the United States warned it would raise tariffs on Indian goods to 25 per cent if the two sides fail to agree.

item.title: Costa Rica Bars UN Rapporteur Francesca Albanese Over Alleged Terror-Links Alert
item.description: Costa Rica has refused entry to Francesca Albanese, the United Nations special rapporteur for the occupied Palestinian territories, saying she is named in an international alert over alleged links to terrorist acts, a claim she has dismissed as a disgrace.

item.title: Babahoyo Under Water as Ecuador Flood Toll Climbs to at Least 30
item.description: Floods driven by heavy El Niño rains have left much of the Ecuadorian city of Babahoyo under water, with at least 30 people now dead and more than 121,000 affected across the country.

item.title: Marital Rape Still Legal Across Much of South Asia, Leaving Millions of Wives Unprotected, Report Finds
item.description: Millions of married women across South Asia have no legal protection against rape by their husbands, a new regional report has found, with the law in five of the region's eight countries still treating forced sex inside marriage as no crime at all.

item.title: Spain Votes on Sunday in Snap Election That Could Bring the Far Right to Power
item.description: Spaniards head to the polls on Sunday in a snap general election that could hand the far right a share of power for the first time since Spain became a democracy after Franco.

item.title: Kenyan Man Wrongly Sentenced to Death Over Attack on British Couple Sues London's Metropolitan Police
item.description: A Kenyan woodcutter who spent more than a decade in prison after being wrongly sentenced to death over a 2011 attack on a British couple says London's Metropolitan Police destroyed his life, as he sues the force over the evidence that put him behind bars.

item.title: Makkah Pact Nations Open Two-Day Talks in Islamabad as Yemen War Tops the Agenda
item.description: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have opened two days of talks in Islamabad to turn their mutual defence pact into a working alliance, with the war between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis on the agenda.

item.title: New Zealand's Ruling Coalition Loses Its Majority in Final Count, Leaving a Hung Parliament
item.description: New Zealand's ruling coalition has lost its parliamentary majority in the final election count, leaving Prime Minister Christopher Luxon dependent on a small centrist party to stay in power.

item.title: Zelenskyy Warns of Major Russian Attack on Power Grid as Trump Tells Putin to Pull Back
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that Russia is preparing another major attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, as US President Donald Trump urged Vladimir Putin to pull back military aggression across Europe.

item.title: One Worker Killed as Projectile Hits Saudi Arabia's Jazan Oil Refinery
item.description: A projectile struck Saudi Aramco's Jazan oil refinery in southwestern Saudi Arabia on Thursday, killing a Nepali worker and injuring several others, the Saudi Energy Ministry said.

item.title: Trump Says Victory Over Iran Is at Hand and Offers Tehran a Chance to Make a Deal
item.description: President Donald Trump told American troops on Thursday that the United States has "victory at hand" in its war on Iran, while offering Tehran another chance to reach a deal and avoid further bloodshed.

item.title: Zelenskyy Says US Is Too Focused on the Middle East and Not Pressing Russia Hard Enough
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused the United States of focusing too much on the Middle East and not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks, saying delays in delivering anti-ballistic missiles are costing Ukrainian lives.

item.title: CIA Waterboarded More Detainees Than It Admitted, Newly Released Files Suggest
item.description: The CIA may have waterboarded more detainees than the three it has officially acknowledged, according to newly released documents that describe an additional case at a secret prison in Afghanistan.

item.title: Israel Threatens New Gaza Operation That Would Displace One Million People
item.description: Israel's defence minister has threatened a new military operation in Gaza that would force one million Palestinians from their homes, unless Hamas hands over its weapons.

item.title: Huntingdon Train Attacker Guilty of 14 Counts of Attempted Murder
item.description: A man who stabbed ten people on a London-bound train at the end of a 24-hour knife rampage has been found guilty of 14 counts of attempted murder, after a four-week trial at Cambridge Crown Court.

item.title: US Judge Blocks FCC Early Review of ABC Station Licenses
item.description: A federal judge in Washington has barred the Federal Communications Commission from carrying out an early review of the licenses of eight Disney-owned ABC television stations, ruling that the move looked like retaliation against the network for programming the Trump administration disliked.

item.title: Trump Calls Pre-Election GDP Figures 'Fake' and Demands Investigation
item.description: Donald Trump has accused his own Commerce Department of deliberately releasing incorrect economic growth figures before this month's midterm elections, calling the numbers 'fake' and demanding an immediate investigation.

item.title: Guinea-Bissau Junta Delays Elections by Two Years, Extending Military Rule to 2028
item.description: Guinea-Bissau's military rulers have delayed presidential and parliamentary elections by almost two years, pushing back the vote that was supposed to restore civilian rule until November 2028.

item.title: SAP Weighs 10,000 Job Cuts in Push to Rebuild Around AI
item.description: German software group SAP is weighing reductions of at least 10,000 jobs as it reshapes its workforce around artificial intelligence, in what would be its biggest round of cuts in years.

item.title: Teenager's Death in Colombia Raid Fuels Questions Over President's Security Crackdown
item.description: The family of an 18-year-old killed in a military operation in northern Colombia says he was a civilian farmworker, not a fighter, in a case that has become the sharpest test yet of the new president's hardline campaign against armed groups.

item.title: Nearly 100 Labour MPs Urge Burnham to Block Rosebank Oilfield
item.description: Ninety-two Labour MPs, including ministerial aides and frontbenchers, have written to Prime Minister Andy Burnham urging him not to approve drilling at the Rosebank oilfield, in the first big internal revolt of his premiership.

item.title: Two More Tankers Hit Mines Near Khasab, Iran's Guards Say
item.description: Two more oil tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines north of Oman's Khasab port, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Thursday, in the latest attack on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Iran Denies Role in Kuwait Drone Attack That Killed Two Italians
item.description: Iran's armed forces have denied any role in the drone attack on Kuwait that killed two Italian technicians, as Kuwait condemned what it called a flagrant violation of its sovereignty and Italy mourned the two men.

item.title: Great Britain Beat Germany to Reach Davis Cup Semi-Finals for First Time Since 2019
item.description: Great Britain are through to the Davis Cup semi-finals for the first time since 2019 after Henry Patten and Neal Skupski won the deciding doubles against Germany in Bologna, sealing a 2-1 quarter-final victory.

item.title: Germany Arrests Two Iraqis Over Alleged Plot to Attack Cologne Synagogue
item.description: German prosecutors have arrested two Iraqi men accused of belonging to a terrorist group that plotted attacks on Jewish and other targets across Europe, including a synagogue in Cologne.

item.title: UN Tribunal Says UNRWA Lacked Evidence to Dismiss Gaza Aid Worker
item.description: A UN tribunal has found that the agency for Palestinian refugees could not back up its decision to sack a Gaza aid worker, ruling that the evidence behind the dismissal fell short, after Israel accused him of taking part in the 7 October 2023 attacks.

item.title: Depardieu to Face Rape Trial After Paris Court Rejects His Appeal
item.description: A Paris appeal court has ordered French film star Gérard Depardieu to stand trial over the alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018, turning down his attempt to have the case dismissed.

item.title: Ibiza Tanker Found Only Partly Submerged as Crews Watch for Diesel Spill
item.description: The diesel tanker that capsized off Ibiza has been found only partly submerged, with its keel sticking out of the water, as Spanish crews work to stop up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel leaking into the sea.

item.title: US Proposes New Tariffs on 14 Trading Partners as China and EU Push Back
item.description: The United States has proposed new tariffs on imports from 14 trading partners, including China and the European Union, drawing protests from governments across Asia and Europe that say they will negotiate but could hit back.
